Vector Spaces and Linear Transformations:
$R^n$: The set of all $n$-tuples of real numbers. <L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 1><L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 2>

Vector Addition: The operation of adding two vectors in $R^n$ by adding their corresponding components. <L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 1>

Scalar Multiplication: The operation of multiplying a vector in $R^n$ by a scalar, where each component of the vector is multiplied by the scalar. <L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 2>

Linear Combination: A vector $\vec{v}$ expressed as a sum of scalar multiples of other vectors $\vec{u}_1, \vec{u}_2, ..., \vec{u}_k$, i.e., $\vec{v} = c_1 \vec{u}_1 + c_2 \vec{u}_2 + ... + c_k \vec{u}_k$, where $c_i$ are scalars. <L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 5>

Span: The set of all possible linear combinations of a given set of vectors. <L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 6>

Vector Space: A set $V$ on which vector addition and scalar multiplication are defined, satisfying eight specific properties (Slides 8, 9). <L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 8><L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 9><L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 10><L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 11><L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 12><L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 13><L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 14>

$P_n$: The vector space of polynomials of degree at most $n$. <L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 10><L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 11>

$F$: The vector space of all functions $f: R \rightarrow R$. <L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 12>

Composition of Linear Transformations: The sequential application of two or more linear transformations, which can be represented by the multiplication of their corresponding matrices. The composition of transformations $A$ and $B$ is represented by the matrix product $AB$.<L[2024-10-22-MatrixMult] 3><L[2024-10-22-MatrixMult] 4>

Change of Basis: A transformation of a vector from one coordinate system (basis) to another. <L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 4><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 5>
Matrix Algebra:
Coefficient Matrix: A matrix whose entries are the coefficients of the variables in a system of linear equations.<L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 3>

Augmented Matrix: A matrix formed by appending the column vector of constants to the coefficient matrix of a system of linear equations.<L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 3>

Elementary Row Operations: Operations performed on the rows of a matrix that do not change the solution set of the corresponding system of linear equations. These include swapping two rows, multiplying a row by a non-zero scalar, and adding a multiple of one row to another.<L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 4><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 5>

Backward Substitution: A method for solving a system of linear equations represented by an upper triangular matrix, starting from the last equation and substituting the solutions back into the preceding equations.<L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 9><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 10>

Pivot Variables: In a system of linear equations in row echelon form, the variables corresponding to the columns containing the leading 1s.<L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 11><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 12><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 13><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 14><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 15>

Free Variables: In a system of linear equations in row echelon form, the variables corresponding to the columns that do not contain a leading 1.<L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 11><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 12><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 13><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 14><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 15>

$M_{m \times n}$: The vector space of all $m \times n$ matrices. <L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 13><L[2024-09-10-VectorSpace] 14>


Matrix Multiplication: The operation of multiplying a matrix by a vector or another matrix, resulting in a new vector or matrix. The result is obtained by taking the dot product of each row of the first matrix with the column vector (or each column of the second matrix).<L[2024-10-22-MatrixMult] 1><L[2024-10-22-MatrixMult] 2><L[2024-10-22-MatrixMult] 5>

Linearity Properties of Matrix Multiplication:  Properties that describe how matrix multiplication interacts with scalar multiplication and vector addition. Specifically, $A(\alpha X + \beta Y) = \alpha AX + \beta AY$ and $(\alpha A + \beta B)X = \alpha AX + \beta BX$, where $A$ and $B$ are matrices, $X$ and $Y$ are vectors, and $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are scalars.<L[2024-10-22-MatrixMult] 2>

Properties of Matrix Multiplication:  A set of rules governing matrix multiplication, including distributivity over addition, the transpose rule, and the non-commutative nature of matrix multiplication ($AB \neq BA$ in general).<L[2024-10-22-MatrixMult] 6><L[2024-10-22-MatrixMult] 7><L[2024-10-22-MatrixMult] 8>

Identity Matrix: A square matrix with ones along the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere.  Multiplying any matrix by the identity matrix results in the original matrix. <L[2024-10-22-MatrixMult] 7>

Diagonal Matrix: A square matrix where all elements outside the main diagonal are zero. The product of two diagonal matrices is another diagonal matrix where each diagonal element is the product of the corresponding diagonal elements of the original matrices.<L[2024-10-22-MatrixMult] 8>


Eigenvalues: The scalar values $\lambda$ that satisfy the equation $Ax = \lambda x$, where $A$ is a square matrix and $x$ is a non-zero vector.  <L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 1><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 2><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 3><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 8><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 9>

Eigenvectors: The non-zero vectors $x$ that satisfy the equation $Ax = \lambda x$, where $A$ is a square matrix and $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue. <L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 1><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 2><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 3><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 8><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 9>

Diagonalizable Matrix: A square matrix $A$ that can be expressed in the form $A = QDQ^{-1}$, where $Q$ is an invertible matrix whose columns are the eigenvectors of $A$, and $D$ is a diagonal matrix whose diagonal entries are the corresponding eigenvalues of $A$. <L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 1><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 4><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 6>
Markov Chains:
Markov Chain: A stochastic model describing a sequence of possible events where the probability of each event depends only on the state attained in the previous event. <L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 7><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 8><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 9><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 10>

Transition Matrix: A square matrix used in Markov chains, where each entry $a_{ij}$ represents the probability of transitioning from state $i$ to state $j$. <L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 7><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 8><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 9><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 10>

Steady-State Distribution: The long-term probability distribution of a Markov chain, which is independent of the initial state. <L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 10>

Systems of Linear Equations:
Solving Systems of Linear Equations: This problem involves finding the values of variables that satisfy a given set of linear equations. Determining the solution type of a system of linear equations: This problem focuses on identifying whether a system of linear equations has a unique solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solution, based on the row echelon form or reduced row echelon form of its augmented matrix. <L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 18><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 19><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 20>

Expressing pivot variables in terms of free variables: This problem involves expressing the pivot variables of a system of linear equations in terms of its free variables after transforming the system's augmented matrix into row echelon form. <L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 12><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 13><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 14><L[2024-08-22-GaussianElimination] 15>

Converting to Standard Form:  The process of transforming a linear programming problem into a standard form, involving the introduction of slack variables to convert inequalities to equalities and ensuring all variables are non-negative. <L[2024-09-05-ColNullSpaces] 3>

Pivot Selection Rules:  The rules for selecting the entering and leaving variables during a pivot operation in the simplex method, involving identifying the most negative coefficient in the objective row and the smallest non-negative ratio of RHS values to coefficients of the entering variable. <L[2024-09-05-ColNullSpaces] 7>

Homogeneous vs. Inhomogeneous Systems: The distinction between homogeneous ($Ax = 0$) and inhomogeneous ($Ax = b$) linear systems, focusing on their solution spaces and the condition for the existence of solutions in inhomogeneous systems. <L[2024-09-05-ColNullSpaces] 17>

Finding a Particular Solution: The process of finding a vector $x_p$ that satisfies $Ax_p = b$, emphasizing the condition that $b$ must be in the column space of $A$ for a solution to exist. <L[2024-09-05-ColNullSpaces] 18><L[2024-09-05-ColNullSpaces] 21><L[2024-09-05-ColNullSpaces] 22>

Uniqueness and Existence of Solutions: The conditions for the existence and uniqueness of solutions to $Ax = b$, stating that existence depends on $b$ being in the column space of $A$ and uniqueness depends on the null space of $A$ containing only the zero vector. <L[2024-09-05-ColNullSpaces] 23>

Diagonalizing a Matrix: Finding a matrix $Q$ and a diagonal matrix $D$ such that $A = QDQ^{-1}$, where $A$ is the given matrix, $Q$ is a matrix whose columns are the eigenvectors of $A$, and $D$ is a diagonal matrix whose diagonal entries are the eigenvalues of $A$. <L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 1><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 2><L[2024-11-26-DiagAppls] 3>

Linear Systems of Equations:
Gaussian Elimination: This algorithm solves a system of linear equations by performing elementary row operations to transform the augmented matrix into row echelon form, then back-substitution to find the solution. <L[2024-08-20-ThreeInterpretationsLinSys] 14>

Substitution Method: This algorithm solves a system of linear equations by solving one equation for one variable in terms of the others, and then substituting this expression into the other equations to reduce the number of variables.  This process is repeated until a single equation with one variable remains, which is then solved. The solution is then back-substituted into the previous equations to find the values of the other variables. <L[2024-08-20-ThreeInterpretationsLinSys] 1>

Pivot Operation: This operation updates the simplex tableau by selecting an entering and leaving variable, and then performing row operations to make the pivot element 1 and all other elements in the entering variable's column 0. <L[2024-09-05-ColNullSpaces] 8>

Linear Combination of Vectors: This algorithm expresses a given vector as a linear combination of other vectors by solving a system of linear equations whose coefficients are the weights of the linear combination. <L[2024-08-20-ThreeInterpretationsLinSys] 3><L[2024-08-20-ThreeInterpretationsLinSys] 11>

Linear Transformation: This algorithm maps a vector from one vector space to another using a matrix multiplication.
